Theme

Church life · Time, the calendar & feasts

the Ascension noun

also Ascension, Ascension Day

medieval

M-O s.v. Christian: Ascension (Day): diēs Ascēnsiōnis Chrīstī in caelum (Tursellinus, 1652)

Ascēnsiō, Ascēnsiōnis f.

noun, third declension

Classically an ascent (ascēnsiō, Plaut.; Lewis & Short); the feast forty days after Easter, a Thursday, in both churches. Lewis & Short do not give the feast’s name.

Examples

  • assūmptus est in caelum, et sedet ā dextrīs Deī

    he was taken up into heaven, and sits at the right hand of GodVulg. Mc. 16.19

  • ēgressus ejus ā Patre, regressus ejus ad Patrem, excursus ūsque ad īnferōs, recursus ad sēdem Deī

    his going out from the Father, his going back to the Father, his journey down to the dead, his return to God’s throneAmbr. hymn. Intende 21–24

See also Easter, Pentecost, heaven.

SourcesLewis & Short: ascensio

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Christian: Ascension (Day).
